source_text: Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο καὶ σωμάτων ἀνάστασιν ἔσεσθαι πεπιστεύκαμεν μετὰ τὴν τῶν ὅλων συντέλειαν, οὐχ ὡς οἱ Στωϊκοὶ δογματίζουσι κατά τινας κύκλων περιόδους, γινομένων ἀεὶ καὶ ἀπογινομένων τῶν αὐτῶν οὐκ ἐπί τι χρήσιμον, ἅπαξ δέ, τῶν καθ᾿ ἡμᾶς αἰώνων πεπερασμένων, καὶ εἰς τὸ παντελὲς διὰ μόγων τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὴν σύστασιν ἔσεσθαι χάριν κρίσεως. Δικάζουσι δὲ ἡμῖν οὐ Μίνως οὐδὲ Ῥαδάμανθυς, ὧν πρὸ τῆς τελευτῆς οὐδεμία τῶν ψυχῶν ὡς μυθολογοῦσιν ἐκρίνετο· δοκιμαστὴς δὲ αὐτὸς ὁ ποιητὴς θεὸς γίνεται. Κἂν γὰρ πάνυ φληνάφους καὶ σπερμολόγους ἡμᾶς νομίσητε, μέλον οὐκ ἔστιν ἡμῖν, ἐπεὶ τούτῳ τῷ λόγῳ πεπιστεύκαμεν. Ὥσπερ γὰρ οὐκ ὢν πρὶν ἢ γενέσθαι τίς ἤμην οὐκ ἐγίνωσκον, μόνον δὲ ἐν ὑποστάσει τῆς σαρκικῆς ὕλης ὑπῆρχον, γεγονὼς δὲ ὁ μὴ πάλαι διὰ τῆς γενέσεως τὸ εἶναι πεπίστευκα· τὸν αὐτὸν τρόπον ὁ γενόμενος καὶ διὰ θανάτου μηκέτι ὤν, αὖθίς τε μηκέθ᾿ ὁρώμενος, ἔσομαι πάλιν, ὥσπερ μὴ πάλαι γεγονὼς εἶτα γεννηθείς. Κἂν πῦρ ἐξαφανίσῃ μου τὸ σαρκίον, ἐξατμισθεῖσαν τὴν ὕλην ὁ κόσμος κεχώρηκεν· κἂν ἐν ποταμοῖς, κἂν ἐν θαλάτταις ἐκδαπανηθῶ, κἂν ὑπὸ θηρίων διασπασθῶ, ταμείοις ἐναπόκειμαι πλουσίου δεσπότου. Καὶ ὁ μὲν πτωχὸς καὶ ἄθεος οὐκ οἶδε τὰ ἀποκείμενα· θεὸς δὲ ὁ βασιλεύων, ὅτε βούλεται, τὴν ὁρατὴν αὐτῷ μόνῳ ὑπόστασιν ἀποκαταστήσει πρὸς τὸ ἀρχαῖον.
pass_a_gloss: And because of this we have believed that there will be a resurrection of bodies after the completion of all things, not as the Stoics dogmatize according to certain cycles, always coming into being and passing away of the same things to no useful purpose, but once, since the ages pertaining to us have been completed, and the constitution will be for the sake of judgment through the deeds of men. And they do not judge us, neither Minos nor Rhadamanthus, since before their death none of the souls were judged as they mythologize; but the Creator God himself becomes the judge. And even if you consider us to be foolish and talkative, it is not a concern to us, since we have believed in this word. For just as I was not before I came into being and did not know that I was someone, but only existed in the substance of fleshly matter, and having come into being, I have believed in being through birth; in the same way, the one who has come into being and through death is no longer, and again will not be seen, I will be again, just as if I had not come into being before and then was born. And even if fire destroys my flesh, the world has absorbed the evaporated matter; and even if I am dissolved in rivers or in seas, or torn apart by wild beasts, I am laid up in the storehouses of a rich Master. And the poor and godless man does not know the things that have been laid up; but God, the reigning King, when he wishes, will restore the visible substance, visible only to him, to its original state.

choices.english: the Creator God himself becomes the judge

pass_b_english: Because of this, we believe that bodies will be raised after the completion of all things, but not in the way the Stoics teach. They claim that the same things come into being and pass away in endless cycles, serving no useful purpose. We hold instead that this will happen once, because the ages allotted to us have reached their end, and the final constitution of things will take place for the sake of judgment through the deeds of men. We will not be judged by Minos or Rhadamanthus; in their myths no soul was judged before death, but the Creator God himself becomes the judge. Even if you consider us foolish and chattering, we are not concerned, for we have put our trust in this word. Just as I did not exist before I was born — I had no awareness of being anyone, but only existed in the substance of fleshly matter — and having come into being, I found existence through birth; so also, though I cease to be and am no longer seen through death, I will be again, just as I was not before and then was born. If fire consumes my flesh, the world receives the evaporated matter; if I am dissolved in rivers or seas, or torn apart by wild beasts, I am stored in the treasuries of a rich Master. The poor and godless man does not know what has been laid up, but God the reigning King, when he wills, will restore the visible substance that only he can see to its original state.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the distinction between Stoic cyclicality and the Christian linear view of judgment. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek source. The translation of 'μόγων' as 'deeds' and 'ποιητὴς' as 'Creator' is appropriate for the context.
